content.text:
The drawing is a biphenyl carboxylic acid linked through a hydrazone to an N-aryl oxindole.

**Left ring system.** The top-left ring carries CO2H and is attached to the second ring, so the acid sits meta to the biaryl bond. On the second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring is adjacent to the carbon bearing OH. The next carbon along bears the NH–N= group, so the ring reads biaryl carbon, C–OH, C–NH, with the remaining three CH.

**Hydrazone and oxindole.** The NH is joined to N, which is double-bonded to C3 of the oxindole. C3 is bonded to C2 (C=O), then N1, which carries the aryl group. The fused benzene ring completes the oxindole. The N-aryl group is a 4-fluoro-3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond has a geometry implied by the drawing. At the C3 end, the C=N carbon has the C=O side (C2) on one side and the benzo ring (C3a) on the other. N is drawn at upper left of C3, with NH pointing down-left from N. The C=O is at lower left of C3 and the benzo ring is to the right. The N substituent (NH) goes left/up from N, toward the same side as C2 (the carbonyl), so the NH and C2 are on the same side (Z).

**SMILES construction.** Writing the hydrazone as N/N=C3/... requires tracking the bond directions:

- `Oc1c(c2cccc(C(=O)O)c2)cccc1N/N=C3\C(=O)N(c4ccc(F)c(C(F)(F)F)c4)c5ccccc35`
- Here the fragment `N/N=C3\C(=O)`: the N before the slash is "below" N=, and the C(=O) after the backslash is "below" C3 as well, so NH and C2 are on the same side, which is Z.

SMILES: Oc1c(c2cccc(C(=O)O)c2)cccc1N/N=C3\C(=O)N(c4ccc(F)c(C(F)(F)F)c4)c5ccccc35
